[THE BIGGER LABOR MARKET]{.eyebrow}

## Growth, with the right context.

::: {.section-intro}
Compare national occupations that overlap with commercial analytics work. These benchmarks include all industries and experience levels; they are not expected certificate starting salaries.
:::

[BLS · {{< var projection_period >}} projections · May {{< var wage_year >}} wages]{.pill}

```{ojs}
//| output: false
benchmarks = FileAttachment("outputs/us-employer-inventory/web/outlook-data.json").json()
occupations = benchmarks.occupations
metricLabels = new Map([["Projected growth (%)", "growth"], ["Median annual wage ($)", "median"], ["Annual projected openings", "openings"]])
formatMetric = (value, key) => key === "median" ? "$" + value.toLocaleString("en-US") : key === "growth" ? value + "%" : value.toLocaleString("en-US")
comparison = occupations.filter(d => selectedOccupations.includes(d.name)).sort((a, b) => b[metric] - a[metric])
```

::: {.panel .analytics-controls}
### Choose your comparison

```{ojs}
viewof selectedOccupations = Inputs.checkbox(occupations.map(d => d.name), {label: "Occupations", value: occupations.map(d => d.name)})
viewof metric = Inputs.select(metricLabels, {label: "Compare", value: "growth"})
```
:::

::: {#growth-chart .native-cards}
### Occupation comparison

```{ojs}
comparison.length ? html`<div class="outlook-grid">${comparison.map(d => html`<article class="benchmark-card">
  <span class="tiny">SOC ${d.soc} · NATIONAL PROXY</span>
  <h3>${d.name}</h3>
  <strong class="benchmark-growth">${metric === "growth" && d.growth > 0 ? "+" : ""}${formatMetric(d[metric], metric)}</strong>
  <p class="tiny">${metric === "growth" ? `projected growth, ${benchmarks.projection_period}` : metric === "median" ? `May ${benchmarks.wage_year} median annual wage` : `average annual projected openings, ${benchmarks.projection_period}`}</p>
  <div class="growth-track" aria-hidden="true"><span style=${`width:${100 * d[metric] / Math.max(1, ...occupations.map(o => o[metric]))}%`}></span></div>
  <div class="benchmark-facts">
    <div><strong>${formatMetric(d.median, "median")}</strong><small>Median annual wage</small></div>
    <div><strong>${formatMetric(d.openings, "openings")}</strong><small>Annual projected openings</small></div>
  </div>
  <p class="tiny">${d.growth}% projected growth · ${benchmarks.projection_period}. Openings include replacement needs, not currently advertised jobs.</p>
  <a href=${d.url} target="_blank" rel="noopener">BLS source ↗</a> · <a href=${d.onet} target="_blank" rel="noopener">O*NET occupation ↗</a>
</article>`)}</div>` : html`<p role="status">Select at least one occupation to compare.</p>`
```

::: {.tiny}
Change the measure to update the highlighted figures and comparison tracks. Cards and the table follow your occupation selection. Tracks use the highest value across all benchmark occupations, so filtering does not change their scale.
:::
:::

::: {.panel .analytics-table}
### Compare the numbers

Click a column heading to sort. The table follows your occupation selection.

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(comparison, {
  select: false, rows: 10, maxHeight: 340, layout: "auto",
  columns: ["name", "soc", "growth", "median", "openings", "url", "onet"],
  header: {name: "Occupation", soc: "SOC", growth: "Growth (%)", median: "Median wage", openings: "Annual openings", url: "BLS", onet: "O*NET"},
  format: {growth: d => d + "%", median: d => formatMetric(d, "median"), openings: d => d.toLocaleString("en-US"), url: d => html`<a href=${d} target="_blank" rel="noopener">Source ↗</a>`, onet: d => html`<a href=${d} target="_blank" rel="noopener">Tasks ↗</a>`}
})
```

::: {.tiny}
Openings include replacement needs; they are not currently advertised jobs. Growth covers {{< var projection_period >}}; wages are May {{< var wage_year >}} medians.
:::

::: {.comparison-note}
### How METEOR compares

BLS estimates employment and projected growth. METEOR observes advertisements in a changing collection. O*NET describes work. Their different populations provide complementary views of careers, rather than a common vacancy-rate measure.

[View the comparison framework →](eda_pharma.qmd#comparison)
